Note::reshape¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::reshape(pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> sizes) const

sizes accepts any contiguous integer range — a braced list {2, 3}, a std::vector<std::int64_t>, a std::array, or a std::span.

Reinterpret The Same Cells Under A New Shape¶

reshape() returns a Note that holds exactly the same cells in the same row-major order but presents them with a different rank and axis sizes. It is the tool for turning a flat list of strings into a grid, collapsing a grid back to a list, or adding a leading batch axis before a shape-sensitive operation.

Nothing about the text is touched: no cell is copied, concatenated, or re-encoded, and the bytes-vs-UTF-8 mode carries over. Only the shape metadata changes, so the call is O(numel) at most (it duplicates the small offset table) and never does per-string work.

The sizes contract¶

  • Rank 0 to 3. A four-or-more-element sizes raises Note supports up to 3D. An empty sizes ({}) targets a 0-D scalar and requires numel() == 1.

  • The product must equal numel. A mismatch raises reshape numel mismatch.

  • One dimension may be -1, and is inferred as numel() / (product of the other dimensions). Two -1s raise reshape allows at most one inferred (-1) dimension; a -1 whose partner product does not divide numel() raises reshape cannot infer the -1 dimension: total element count is not divisible by the other dimensions.

  • Every other dimension must be ≥ 0; a 0 is allowed and yields an empty Note.

Row-major reinterpretation¶

Cells are stored last-axis-fastest. reshape walks that same linear sequence and re-groups it: ["a","b","c","d","e","f"] reshaped to {2, 3} fills row 0 with a b c and row 1 with d e f. It does not transpose — for that use transpose or permute.

Example 1: List To Grid¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.reshape({2, 3})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "c"], 
  ["d", "e", "f"]
]

Example 2: Adding A Leading Axis¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.reshape({1, 2, 3})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2, 3], dim=3, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  [
    ["a", "b", "c"], 
    ["d", "e", "f"]
  ]
]

Example 3: Regrouping A Grid¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.reshape({3, 2})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3, 2], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b"], 
  ["c", "d"], 
  ["e", "f"]
]

The 2 × 3 grid and the 3 × 2 grid are the same six cells read in the same order — only the row boundaries move.

Example 4: Inferring A Dimension With -1¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.reshape({-1, 3})) << "\n";   // rows inferred as 2
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.reshape({2, -1})) << "\n";   // cols inferred as 3

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "c"], 
  ["d", "e", "f"]
]
Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "c"], 
  ["d", "e", "f"]
]

Example 5: Reshaping To A 0-D Scalar¶

const auto s = pluss::make_note("solo");
std::cout << s.reshape({1}).reshape(std::vector<std::int64_t>{}) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"solo"

A one-element Note round-trips between rank 0 and rank 1 freely.

Example 6: Rejections¶

auto first_line = [](const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string m = e.what();
  return m.substr(0, m.find('\n'));
};

try { (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c"}).reshape({2, 2}); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d"}).reshape({-1, -1}); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e"}).reshape({-1, 2}); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b"}).reshape({1, 1, 1, 2}); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

Output¶

reshape numel mismatch
reshape allows at most one inferred (-1) dimension
reshape cannot infer the -1 dimension: total element count is not divisible by the other dimensions
Note supports up to 3D

See Also¶

  • Note::flatten: the common case — reshape to rank 1.

  • Note::squeeze / Note::unsqueeze: drop or add a single size-1 axis without restating the whole shape.

  • Note::transpose / Note::permute: reorder axes (which does move cells) rather than regroup them.
